A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ThinkLite-VL and contain readable text, equations, figures, and tables. Material moved from v1 into v2's Appendices A–C can be matched reliably, supporting comparison of the complete work.

before.justification: v1 reports original ThinkLite-VL-7B evaluations on eight benchmarks, sample-selection ablations, training reward curves, and difficulty analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds 72B evaluations, online-filtering comparisons, and experiments transferring selected training sets between models.

M1.justification: The proposed MCTS search, difficulty criterion, critic, and GRPO objective remain unchanged. Both select samples requiring more than five iterations plus those unsolved after 50 iterations. Applying this procedure to a 72B model introduces another model configuration, without a documented algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight-source, approximately 70k training pool and the same eight evaluation benchmarks. The new 7.5k subset and cross-model experiments change sample selection and model configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main eight-benchmark comparison adds LLaVA-Onevision-7B/72B, InternVL2.5-8B, and QvQ-72B (v1 Table 5 versus v2 Table 2). Section 4.3 also introduces an online self-consistency selection comparator. Existing principal comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds 72B training on 7.5k selected samples with a matched random-selection control, online filtering retaining rollout accuracy between 0 and 0.9, and training each model on the other's selected subset. MM-EUREKA's reported training size changes from 54k to 15k. Vision-R1 changes from explicitly paper-reported results to v2's stated common-code evaluation; these reporting changes do not independently establish reruns.

E4.justification: New Sections 4.3–4.4 test online versus offline filtering and whether selected data transfer between model sizes. They add subset-overlap analysis and cross-sample training (Tables 4–5). The original reward curves, difficulty-threshold ablation, and case studies remain in Appendices B–C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Results remain point estimates; rollout counts describe training and selection procedures rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive 72B, comparator, online-filtering, and cross-model results. ThinkLite-VL-7B's MathVerse, MMMU, and average scores change from 50.7, 54.6, and 63.89 to 52.1, 55.5, and 64.18. Qwen2.5-VL-72B's reported average changes from 70.81 to 68.25; these are reported revisions, not established same-setting gains or losses. v2 also contains inconsistencies: Appendix B retains 63.89, and Table 2's 72B random-control improvement is 3.06 although its averages imply 2.76.

T1.justification: The state/action definitions, visitation-based selection formula, and GRPO objective in Equation 1 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on an 11k-sample 7B model. v2 presents a scalable 7B/72B model family, extending the headline claims to 7.5k-sample 72B training and reported SoTA scores of 79.7 on MathVista and 64.3 on MathVerse. The original difficulty-guided, distillation-free self-improvement claim remains.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 introduces an important applicability boundary: selected datasets transfer poorly between models, even from stronger to weaker models. It interprets asymmetric difficulty as evidence of different reasoning heuristics and motivates model-specific filtering. Section 4.3 additionally argues that online filtering mainly accelerates convergence without replacing effective difficulty identification.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 8×80GB A100 hardware, vLLM inference, common evaluation code, and model-provided thinking templates. It also explicitly promises both model sizes and their filtered datasets. Existing prompts and selection parameters are retained, with prompts relocated to Appendix A; the resource URL remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to PagedAttention/vLLM, LLaVA-OneVision, Qwen2-VL, and DAPO. Related work more explicitly distinguishes training-data selection from inference-time MCTS and adds a first-framework claim for combining search-based difficulty estimation with RFT. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction are rewritten, a five-item contribution list is introduced, and evaluation discussion is reorganized around two model sizes. Prompts, reward/difficulty analyses, and case studies move into structured Appendices A–C, substantially changing the document's organization.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, and the main benchmark table gains model-category sections and colored improvement rows. New Tables 4–5 display online-filtering and cross-model comparisons. Numerous retained prompt, ablation, and case-study displays move into the appendices, separating examples from the conclusion and references.

improvement.justification: The 72B random-control comparisons and new online-filtering and transfer analyses strengthen the evidence for sample selection and clarify its model-specific limits. The reorganized appendices also improve readability. However, conflicting 7B averages and the incorrect 72B improvement calculation weaken reporting reliability. These inconsistencies do not reverse the displayed comparisons, but limit the net quality gain.
